lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately

s.t: Our operations are grouped into three reportable segments: Mountain, Lodging and Real Estate, which represented approximately 88%, 12% and 0%, respectively, of our net revenue for our fiscal year ended July 31, 2026 (“Fiscal 2026”).
For Fiscal 2026, our pass products generated approximately 70% of our total lift revenue and approximately 73% of total visitation (excluding complimentary access).

This seasonality is partially mitigated by the sale of pass products (which for Fiscal 2026 accounted for approximately 70% of the total lift revenue) predominately occurring during the period prior to the start of the ski season as the cash from those sales is collected in advance and revenue is primarily recognized in the second and third fiscal quarters.
The Mountain, Lodging and Real Estate segments represented approximately 88%, 12% and 0%, respectively, of our net revenue for Fiscal 2026.
Approximately 70%, 65% and 65% of total lift revenue was derived from pass revenue for Fiscal 2026, Fiscal 2025 and Fiscal 2024, respectively.

Our business relies on the continuous operation of information technology systems and services.
We also provide information to third party service providers and rely on third party service providers for the provision of information technology services.
Our business relies on the use of large volumes of data.

Our ability to fund capital expenditures will depend on our ability to generate sufficient cash flow from operations and/or to borrow from third parties in the debt market or raise additional capital in the equity market.
Our ability to generate cash flow and to obtain third-party financing will depend upon many factors, including:
We rely on various government permits and landlord approvals at our U.S. resorts.
We rely on foreign government leases and landlord approvals, and are subject to certain related laws and regulations, at our international resorts.
Perisher relies on a suite of planning approvals (and existing use rights) granted under the Australian EPA Act to operate the resort.

We rely on information technology to operate our businesses and maintain our competitiveness, and any failure to adapt to technological developments or industry trends, including the usage of AI technologies, could harm our business or competitive position.

We depend on the use of sophisticated information technology and systems for central reservations, point of sale, marketing, customer relationship management and communication, procurement, maintaining the privacy of guest and employee data, administration and technologies we make available to our guests.

The timing and amount of repurchases, if any, will depend upon several factors, including market and business conditions, our liquidity and capital resources, the trading price of our common stock and the nature of other investment opportunities.

Our largest source of Mountain segment revenue comes from the sale of lift tickets (including pass products), which represented approximately 58%, 57% and 57% of Mountain segment net revenue for Fiscal 2026, the fiscal year ended July 31, 2025 (“Fiscal 2025”) and the fiscal year ended July 31, 2024 (“Fiscal 2024”), respectively.
The geographic mix depends on levels of visitation to our destination mountain resorts versus our regional ski areas.
Our long-term liquidity needs depend upon operating results, which in turn impact the borrowing capacity under our credit agreements.
The accounting for changes in fair value of hedging instruments depends on the effectiveness of the hedge.
